content.title: The Constraint Cheat Sheet — MEMORISE THIS
content.text:
N ≤ 12        → O(n!) or O(2^n × n)  — Backtracking/Bitmask DP
N ≤ 20        → O(2^n)               — Bitmask / meet-in-middle
N ≤ 500       → O(n³)                — Floyd-Warshall, 3-loop DP
N ≤ 5000      → O(n²)                — Quadratic DP, Dijkstra naive
N ≤ 10^5      → O(n log n)           — Sort, Binary search, Segment tree
N ≤ 10^6      → O(n) or O(n log n)   — Linear scan, Sieve
N ≤ 10^9      → O(√n) or O(log n)    — Math tricks
N ≤ 10^18     → O(log n)             — Binary search, matrix exponentiation
4.3  How to Calculate Complexity
Rules
Drop constants: O(2n) = O(n)
Drop lower terms: O(n² + n) = O(n²)
Nested loops multiply: outer O(n) × inner O(n) = O(n²)
Sequential operations add then simplify: O(n) + O(n²) = O(n²)
Recursion: T(n) = work + T(subproblem); solve by recursion tree or Master Theorem
Master Theorem (for Divide & Conquer)

code: T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n)  where a≥1, b>1
Case 1: f(n) = O(n^c) where c < log_b(a)  →  T(n) = O(n^log_b(a))
Case 2: f(n) = O(n^c) where c = log_b(a)  →  T(n) = O(n^c log n)
Case 3: f(n) = O(n^c) where c > log_b(a)  →  T(n) = O(f(n))
a=2, b=2, log_2(2)=1, f(n)=O(n^1) → Case 2 → O(n log n) ✓

code: START: What is the core structure?
│   ├── Contiguous subarray sum/max/min? → Sliding Window or Kadane

│   └── All valid placements → Backtracking with pruning

├── K closest / K largest → Heap (Priority Queue)
└── Number theory → GCD, Sieve, modular arithmetic

content.text: Section 7 — Master Cheat Sheet Summary
Prefix Sum: O(1) range queries after O(n) build — always go-to for range sums
Kadane: max subarray in O(n) — the most asked array problem
Two Pointers: O(n) for sorted arrays — reduce O(n²) to O(n)
Sliding Window: O(n) for subarray/substring constraints
Binary Search on Answer: whenever answer is monotonic
Monotonic Stack: O(n) for NGE, NSE, histogram — deceptively powerful
DSU: O(α(n)) connectivity — Kruskal's MST, cycle detection
Dijkstra: O((V+E)log V) — most asked graph problem
Backtracking: always undo your choice after recursive call
DP: identify state, transition, base case — then code top-down or bottom-up
